official_admissions.title: Bank capital, lending, and regulation: A meta-analysis

jif.verification: Wiley journal metrics / publisher journal page (current metric safely above project floor)

full_text.source: Wiley version plus publicly attached author/published full-text copies at university repositories
full_text.scope: All substantive argumentative sections available in the full article/public full-version were reviewed: framing/theory, design/method, main results, robustness or heterogeneity where present, discussion/conclusion, and limitations/boundaries. Tables/equations were inspected when needed to calibrate claims.

summary_architecture: construct meta-analytic evidence universe of 1,600+ estimates
separate capital-ratio levels from changes in capital requirements
close with limits on policy-ready effect-size claims
rhetoric.evidence_order: The review separates the relationship between bank capital levels and lending from the effect of changes in regulatory requirements before synthesizing moderators and publication bias.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Effect sizes matter because the sign/magnitude differ by the exact capital construct. Numbers establish that level relationships and regulatory-change effects are not interchangeable.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: Meta-analysis supports pooled associations/effects conditional on underlying designs; it does not turn heterogeneous primary studies into one structural mechanism.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: Post-crisis period, capital definition, empirical method, and regulatory context materially change estimates.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: A literature can have a directional pooled result and still fail to provide a sufficiently stable effect size for policy calibration.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Bank-capital ratio, regulatory capital ratio, and changes in capital requirements are related but distinct constructs across heterogeneous studies.
rhetoric.limitations: Publication bias, modeling choices, time variation, and primary-study design heterogeneity bound policy generalization.
rhetoric.implications: Finance summaries should not use 'more bank capital' and 'higher capital requirements' as grammatical substitutes when the evidence shows different lending relationships.
anti_patterns: Do not collapse a level variable and a policy-induced change into one financial condition.
Do not treat a pooled average as policy-ready when study design materially determines estimates.

atomic_observations.observation: A variable's level and an imposed change in that variable are different evidentiary objects and can have different or opposite relationships with outcomes; prose should not treat them as interchangeable.
A literature can support a broad directional relationship while remaining too heterogeneous to supply a reliable policy effect size.
Finance language should distinguish bank capital levels, regulatory ratios, capital requirements, and changes in requirements.
Meta-analytic synthesis should decompose capital constructs and empirical contexts before stating an aggregate lending conclusion.

official_admissions.title: Short-term financial constraints and SMEs’ investment decision: evidence from the working capital channel

full_text.source: Springer Nature article plus author/repository full version
full_text.scope: All substantive argumentative sections available in the full article/public full-version were reviewed: framing/theory, design/method, main results, robustness or heterogeneity where present, discussion/conclusion, and limitations/boundaries. Tables/equations were inspected when needed to calibrate claims.

summary_architecture: define competition between working and fixed capital for cash
rhetoric.evidence_order: The paper establishes the cash-allocation mechanism before using heterogeneous working-capital needs and liquidity to test whether the proposed channel behaves as predicted.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: The useful magnitude comparison is short-term versus long-term constraint importance; subgroup effects show when internal liquidity absorbs the shock.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: The mechanism is supported by predicted heterogeneity but hidden treatment-selection bias cannot be completely ruled out; mechanism wording should remain calibrated to the design.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: Higher working-capital needs amplify the investment effect; liquid firms that can adjust receivables/inventories are less exposed.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: The article separates cash-credit and investment-credit constraints rather than treating any finance denial as the same event.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: French SME/manufacturing-heavy survey setting; treatment assignment can contain unobserved factors; unquoted firms require accounting proxies.
rhetoric.limitations: Authors explicitly note non-representative sector composition and inability to guarantee absence of hidden bias.
rhetoric.implications: Internal liquidity is not merely a balance-sheet stock: it can function as a buffer that lets firms meet working-capital needs without sacrificing fixed investment.
anti_patterns: Do not describe all credit constraints as equivalent when short- and long-term finance serve competing uses.
Do not state the working-capital channel more strongly than the identification permits.

atomic_observations.observation: Finance prose can describe working capital and fixed investment as competing uses of finite internal cash, making allocation pressure explicit.
Liquidity changes the strength of the financing-constraint effect; the buffer condition belongs in the interpretation.
Predicted moderator behavior can support a mechanism without fully identifying it.
Hidden-bias and sample-composition limits should be attached to the causal/channel claim they constrain.

official_admissions.title: How does government-backed finance affect SMEs’ crisis predictors?

full_text.review_basis: current-session full-text review cross-checked against inherited prior rhetoric record
full_text.scope: All substantive argumentative sections available in the full article/public full-version were reviewed: framing/theory, design/method, main results, robustness or heterogeneity where present, discussion/conclusion, and limitations/boundaries. Tables/equations were inspected when needed to calibrate claims.

summary_architecture: define guarantee intervention and business-continuity outcomes
rhetoric.evidence_order: Profitability and financial-health outcomes are kept separate, then followed through time before policy interpretation.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: The meaningful quantitative structure is outcome divergence and decay of financial burdens over time, not a single average treatment-effect number.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: Causal language is most justified for the matched difference-in-differences treatment effects and should remain outcome-specific.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: Micro/small firms, services, and direct guarantees show larger magnitudes; financial burdens weaken by year two.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: The paper refuses a simple good/bad judgment: profitability improves while short-run financial equilibrium worsens.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Italian guarantee program, 2010–2018, uniform regulatory context; post-pandemic generalization remains untested.
rhetoric.limitations: Country/program/time boundaries are explicit; benefit-cost conclusions depend on beneficiary selection and intervention design.
rhetoric.implications: The same financing intervention can improve operating performance while temporarily worsening leverage and debt-service strain.
anti_patterns: Do not compress a multi-outcome intervention into 'helped' or 'hurt.'
Do not omit the recovery path when the short-run adverse effect fades.

atomic_observations.observation: An intervention can succeed on one financial objective and deteriorate another; evaluation must remain outcome-specific.
Short-run deterioration followed by medium-term relief should be stated as a time path.
Government-backed finance can be described through profitability additionality, leverage, financial burden, debt sustainability, and business-continuity tradeoffs.
Strong intervention verbs are justified only for outcomes supported by the quasi-experimental design.

official_admissions.title: Small and vulnerable during crises? Firm size and financing constraint dynamics

full_text.scope: All substantive argumentative sections available in the full article/public full-version were reviewed: framing/theory, design/method, main results, robustness or heterogeneity where present, discussion/conclusion, and limitations/boundaries. Tables/equations were inspected when needed to calibrate claims.

summary_architecture: separate pre-crisis constraint level from crisis-induced change
trace post-crisis deleveraging and cash accumulation
rhetoric.evidence_order: The article deliberately distinguishes being more constrained on average from being disproportionately worsened by the crisis.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Comparative differences in baseline probability and crisis interaction answer distinct questions; the paper avoids making size itself the sole vulnerability metric.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: The crisis interaction can be interpreted more strongly than a simple cross-sectional level difference, but bank-side supply information is limited.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: SMEs have worse baseline financing conditions, yet the crisis did not tighten constraints disproportionately by size; constrained firms across sizes recover similarly.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: No disproportionate SME crisis effect is stated as a non-difference in shock response, not as evidence that SMEs are financially unconstrained.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Established German firms; very small/young firms underrepresented; bank-level financing supply cannot be directly linked.
rhetoric.limitations: Administrative detail comes with limited bank-side data and country/startup generalizability.
rhetoric.implications: Cash-buffer building is a post-shock financial adaptation and may substitute for debt even when the underlying firm population is otherwise similar.
anti_patterns: Do not infer shock sensitivity from a worse baseline.
Do not treat size as a complete explanation when risk characteristics and funding alternatives matter.

atomic_observations.observation: A group can have a worse baseline state without experiencing a larger response to a shock; level disparity and shock sensitivity are separate claims.
Crisis and post-crisis periods change the financing interpretation, so the temporal regime belongs in the claim.
Cash accumulation can be described as a financing buffer and potential substitute for debt during recovery.
The conclusion should retain the established-German-firm sample rather than becoming a universal SME claim.

official_admissions.title: ECB unconventional monetary policy and SME access to finance

full_text.scope: All substantive argumentative sections available in the full article/public full-version were reviewed: framing/theory, design/method, main results, robustness or heterogeneity where present, discussion/conclusion, and limitations/boundaries. Tables/equations were inspected when needed to calibrate claims.

summary_architecture: interact policy with leverage and risk measures
separate firm-perceived risk from size/age proxies
rhetoric.evidence_order: Policy stance comes first, then the article asks which firms actually experience easier finance; the answer is conditioned by jurisdiction, leverage, age, and size.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Interaction estimates are meaningful only with the firm/jurisdiction condition attached; broad asset-purchase measures are tested against alternatives.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: The study identifies uneven transmission rather than proving a single bank risk-taking mechanism; firm risk measures and bank behavior are distinct evidentiary objects.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: Leveraged firms in stressed countries, small firms, and young firms remain constrained; effects are insignificant in non-stressed countries and for several risk interactions.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: ‘Little evidence’ that risky firms receive loans under UMP is preserved rather than inverted into a statement that risk-taking never occurs.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Euro-area stressed countries, SAFE survey, 2014–2019; SME financing mix is bank-heavy and debt-security issuance rare.
rhetoric.limitations: Risk measurement, discouraged-borrower definition, and broad versus targeted policy proxies are explicit robustness concerns.
rhetoric.implications: An expansionary policy stance does not imply uniform easing at the borrower level; transmission can be segmented by leverage, geography, size, and age.
anti_patterns: Do not infer borrower-level easing from the aggregate direction of monetary policy.
Do not use a null firm-risk interaction to deny all bank risk-taking mechanisms.

atomic_observations.observation: An aggregate policy regime can produce heterogeneous borrower-level outcomes; the borrower/jurisdiction condition must remain explicit.
Finance prose can distinguish policy stance, bank transmission, borrower leverage, credit constraint, discouraged borrowing, and jurisdiction stress.
'Little evidence' for one risk channel is narrower than evidence that the channel is absent.
Alternative measures of policy stance and firm risk are non-equivalent proxies and should not be silently merged.

full_text.scope: All substantive argumentative sections available in the full article/public full-version were reviewed: framing/theory, design/method, main results, robustness or heterogeneity where present, discussion/conclusion, and limitations/boundaries. Tables/equations were inspected when needed to calibrate claims.

summary_architecture: model firm-side and supply-side determinants jointly
connect innovation commercialization to working-capital pressure
rhetoric.evidence_order: The paper moves from who is constrained to which barriers matter, then to financing instruments that address different stages of the firm's needs.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Probability differences and ranked barriers support relative language; policy relevance is stronger when tied to the financing stage each tool actually addresses.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: Recursive bivariate probit controls modeled endogeneity, but survey perceptions and unobserved firm data limit causal mechanism strength.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: Innovative firms are more constrained; collateral, paperwork, and interest rates matter most; tax incentives are less relevant for immediate liquidity needs.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: No single support instrument is presented as universally adequate because R&D subsidy, credit line, guarantee, and equity solve different financing problems.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Euro-area SAFE survey; self-perceived categorical responses; anonymous survey prevents linking to richer balance-sheet databases.
rhetoric.limitations: Subjective/categorical measures and missing cross-source linkage are explicitly acknowledged.
rhetoric.implications: Financing tools should be described by the cash-flow problem they solve: sunk-expenditure reimbursement, collateralized credit, working-capital liquidity, or equity funding.
anti_patterns: Do not rank financing tools without naming the financing stage/objective.
Do not treat perceived constraint measures as identical to observed balance-sheet constraint.

atomic_observations.observation: A financing instrument's usefulness is function-specific: tax incentives, guarantees, credit lines, and equity address different funding jobs.
Collateral, paperwork, price of credit, guarantees, credit lines, and equity are distinct Finance predicates/objects, not one generic 'access' variable.
Self-perceived financing constraints and observed balance-sheet constraints are non-equivalent measurements.
Measurement limitations should constrain policy/cause language exactly where subjective survey responses are doing the evidentiary work.

official_admissions.title: Banks as Lenders of First Resort: Evidence from the COVID-19 Crisis
official_admissions.journal: The Review of Corporate Finance Studies

full_text.review_basis: current-session full-text review cross-checked against inherited prior rhetoric record
full_text.scope: All substantive argumentative sections available in the full article/public full-version were reviewed: framing/theory, design/method, main results, robustness or heterogeneity where present, discussion/conclusion, and limitations/boundaries. Tables/equations were inspected when needed to calibrate claims.

summary_architecture: locate demand at banks serving large firms
explain how deposits/Fed liquidity/preshock capital supported supply
contrast new origination with drawdown measurement boundary
rhetoric.evidence_order: The event scale is established first; the paper then distinguishes borrower draws on preexisting commitments from banks' ability to fund those draws.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Economically interpretable drawdown scale establishes the shock; weekly/quarterly decompositions answer different questions.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: Bank liquidity/capital evidence supports an accommodation explanation, but weekly data cannot always distinguish new lending from preexisting commitment draws.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: Largest banks/large firms dominate the drawdown shock; preshock bank condition is not a robust constraint in the main large-bank setting.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: ‘Do not find robust evidence’ remains a nonresult rather than proof of no influence.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: COVID liquidity shock; U.S. banks; credit-line utilization; measurement frequency changes ability to distinguish transaction types.
rhetoric.limitations: Inability to separate new originations from drawdowns in some data is directly acknowledged.
rhetoric.implications: A rise in loan balances can reflect borrowers exercising prior commitments rather than lenders choosing to originate new credit.
anti_patterns: Do not interpret balance-sheet loan growth automatically as new lending supply.
Do not turn unstable evidence into evidence of no effect.

atomic_observations.observation: A change in a balance-sheet stock can arise from different underlying transactions; aggregate stock growth should not be assigned to a specific flow without decomposition.
Observed loan balances do not reveal all underlying origination versus commitment-draw mechanics without additional data.
Finance language should distinguish committed credit, line drawdown, new origination, liquidity demand, deposit inflow, and bank funding capacity.
'No robust evidence' is the correct form for unstable bank-condition relationships.

official_admissions.title: Financing constraints and firm-level responses to the COVID-19 pandemic: International evidence
official_admissions.journal: Research in International Business and Finance

full_text.source: PubMed Central full article / Elsevier COVID open-reuse archive
full_text.scope: All substantive argumentative sections available in the full article/public full-version were reviewed: framing/theory, design/method, main results, robustness or heterogeneity where present, discussion/conclusion, and limitations/boundaries. Tables/equations were inspected when needed to calibrate claims.

summary_architecture: compare financial adaptation with operational adjustment
rhetoric.evidence_order: Pre-existing bank-credit constraint is used to sort firms before the shock, then post-shock liquidity outcomes and financing choices are compared.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Probability differences reveal which adaptation channels constrained firms use; source composition matters more than a single 'access to finance' metric.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: Pre-shock constraint status strengthens temporal interpretation but does not make every financing response structurally causal.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: Credit-rationed firms experience greater liquidity/cash-flow problems and delinquency; they rely less on bank funding and more on alternative support channels.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: The study preserves differing responses across bank finance, trade credit, government support, and operational actions.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: World Bank enterprise follow-up surveys across 19 countries; SME-focused pandemic setting.
rhetoric.limitations: Survey design and pandemic-specific institutional responses constrain generalization.
rhetoric.implications: Borrower strain should be expressed through liquidity, delinquency, financing-source substitution, and operational adaptation—not a single binary 'financially constrained' label.
anti_patterns: Do not collapse bank finance, trade credit, grants, and operational adjustment into one response.
Do not allow pre-shock sorting alone to prove every post-shock mechanism.

atomic_observations.observation: Finance prose can distinguish liquidity stress, delinquency, bank-credit access, trade-credit substitution, public support, and operational adjustment.
A broad stress outcome becomes interpretable when decomposed into financing-source and operational responses.
The relevant subject is previously credit-rationed SMEs during a pandemic regime, not firms universally.
Pre-shock status strengthens sequencing but does not by itself identify every response mechanism.

official_admissions.title: Global syndicated lending during the COVID-19 pandemic

full_text.source: PubMed Central full article / published open COVID archive
full_text.scope: All substantive argumentative sections available in the full article/public full-version were reviewed: framing/theory, design/method, main results, robustness or heterogeneity where present, discussion/conclusion, and limitations/boundaries. Tables/equations were inspected when needed to calibrate claims.

summary_architecture: use cross-border variation to separate sides of market
rhetoric.evidence_order: Borrower-side and lender-side exposure enter separately so observed lending outcomes are not attributed to only one side of the transaction.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Loan quantities and spreads jointly help distinguish whether observed changes reflect borrower demand, lender capacity, or both.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: The design attempts to separate supply and demand using asymmetric pandemic exposure; causal language should remain tied to that identification strategy.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: Effects differ with borrower and lender exposure and with cross-border relationships.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: A weak result on one side of the market does not imply the other side is inactive.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Global syndicated-loan market during COVID; exposure measures and cross-border structure define identification.
rhetoric.limitations: Supply and demand remain latent economic forces inferred through exposure design rather than directly observed intentions.
rhetoric.implications: Finance summaries should preserve borrower demand and lender supply as distinct potential sources of the same observed loan outcome.
anti_patterns: Do not assign a loan-quantity change entirely to lenders when borrower demand also moved.
Do not use one observed transaction variable to stand in for both sides of the market.

atomic_observations.observation: A single observed transaction outcome can be jointly generated by two sides of a market; when evidence separates them, supply-side and demand-side drivers should remain distinct.
Finance language should distinguish borrower demand/exposure, lender supply/exposure, syndicated quantity, price/spread, and cross-border channel.
Decomposing an aggregate lending outcome by market side prevents mechanism misattribution.
Distinct borrower and lender channels justify separate grammatical claims before total lending interpretation.

official_admissions.title: Bank concentration, credit access, and corporate cash holdings
official_admissions.journal: Review of Quantitative Finance and Accounting

full_text.scope: All substantive argumentative sections available in the full article/public full-version were reviewed: framing/theory, design/method, main results, robustness or heterogeneity where present, discussion/conclusion, and limitations/boundaries. Tables/equations were inspected when needed to calibrate claims.

summary_architecture: contrast bank market-power and information hypotheses
trace effect over time and by firm characteristics
rhetoric.evidence_order: The main relation is established before mediation; partial mediation is retained rather than presented as complete mechanism closure.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Time-slice coefficients show the relationship becoming more pronounced; the article also notes economic meaning from persistence across many firms rather than only immediate firm-level magnitude.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: SEM supports a mediation pattern, but the article explicitly preserves multiple coexisting mechanisms and observational interpretation.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: Effects grow over time and are stronger for credit-constrained/non-NYSE/high-intangible settings.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: The information channel is not declared absent merely because the market-power channel is more salient on average.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: U.S. public firms 1994–2017; state-level bank concentration; structural-equation mediation.
rhetoric.limitations: Bank-credit access only partially mediates; residual mechanisms remain.
rhetoric.implications: Cash holdings can be a precautionary response to constrained external credit rather than a simple sign of unused capacity.
anti_patterns: Do not turn partial mediation into complete causal explanation.
Do not infer that a less salient competing channel is absent.

atomic_observations.observation: Partial mediation should preserve the residual direct relationship and possibility of additional mechanisms.
A dominant channel does not imply a competing channel is absent.
Corporate cash can be framed as precautionary liquidity linked to external credit access, debt capacity, and banking-market structure.
A financing relationship that strengthens over historical subperiods should not be summarized as a fixed timeless coefficient.

official_admissions.title: The impact of economic policy uncertainty and inflation risk on corporate cash holdings
official_admissions.journal: Review of Quantitative Finance and Accounting

full_text.scope: All substantive argumentative sections available in the full article/public full-version were reviewed: framing/theory, design/method, main results, robustness or heterogeneity where present, discussion/conclusion, and limitations/boundaries. Tables/equations were inspected when needed to calibrate claims.

summary_architecture: estimate separate EPU and inflation relationships
rhetoric.evidence_order: Separate main effects and the interaction are kept distinct; the article then shows that sectors and periods can have different cash responses.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Sign differences among standalone EPU, inflation risk, and joint exposure matter more than a generic statement that 'uncertainty raises cash.'
rhetoric.causal_calibration: GMM addresses endogeneity concerns but does not make each macro variable a fully exogenous structural shock.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: Construction and financial firms differ; presidential terms differ; standalone and joint-risk signs differ.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: Mixed signs are preserved rather than forced into a single uncertainty narrative.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: U.S. firms 2011–2021; macro proxies; sector/political-period interactions.
rhetoric.limitations: Macro proxies and observational/dynamic-panel design constrain mechanism language.
rhetoric.implications: Corporate cash responses can depend on the combination of macro risks rather than the isolated direction of each risk factor.
anti_patterns: Do not collapse main effects and interaction effects into one sign.
Do not say 'uncertainty raises cash' when the measured uncertainty components have mixed standalone relationships.

atomic_observations.observation: Main effects and interactions can point in different directions; the combined state is not a restatement of either component alone.
Finance language should distinguish precautionary cash, inflation risk, policy uncertainty, interest burden, and joint macro-risk exposure.
Mixed empirical signs should outrank a simple theoretical narrative about uncertainty.
Dynamic-panel robustness strengthens association but does not automatically justify structural-shock language.

official_admissions.title: A Meta-Analysis of the Impact of Entrepreneurs’ Gender on their Access to Bank Finance

full_text.review_basis: current-session full-text review cross-checked against inherited prior rhetoric record
full_text.scope: All substantive argumentative sections available in the full article/public full-version were reviewed: framing/theory, design/method, main results, robustness or heterogeneity where present, discussion/conclusion, and limitations/boundaries. Tables/equations were inspected when needed to calibrate claims.

rhetoric.evidence_order: Robust pooled findings come before moderators; inferred social mechanism follows and is explicitly separated from causal proof.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Pooled effect estimates establish baseline bias; moderators explain when the gap is larger without erasing the pooled result.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: The meta-analysis explicitly calls for experimental/quasi-experimental work to identify causal mechanisms.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: Political ideology and empowerment moderate the observed financing gap; publication-period/regulatory context matters.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: Publication-bias tests are reported and findings remain relatively stable, but the literature is not presented as causal proof.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: 31-study evidence base; application selection/confidence, omitted income, evolving bank processes/regulation, macro context.
rhetoric.limitations: Publication bias, causal identification, omitted variables, application selection, and time/regulation are named specifically.
rhetoric.implications: A pooled financing disparity and contextual moderation can be stated strongly while mechanism language stays tentative.
anti_patterns: Do not infer the inverse policy conclusion merely from a moderator.
Do not convert meta-analytic association into causal discrimination mechanism.

atomic_observations.observation: Pooled baseline and contextual moderators should be synthesized as separate evidence layers.
Meta-analytic association supports a robust pattern but not causal mechanism language.
Publication, selection, omitted-variable, and causal limits are most useful when tied to the exact inference they bound.
Finance access should distinguish application/approval, rejection, interest terms, and borrower selection rather than one generic access outcome.

official_admissions.title: Overcoming political risk in developing economies through non-local debt

full_text.review_basis: current-session full-text review cross-checked against inherited prior rhetoric record
full_text.scope: All substantive argumentative sections available in the full article/public full-version were reviewed: framing/theory, design/method, main results, robustness or heterogeneity where present, discussion/conclusion, and limitations/boundaries. Tables/equations were inspected when needed to calibrate claims.

rhetoric.evidence_order: The observed financing-structure response is stated before the claim that the chosen lender mix effectively constrains host-country behavior.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Syndicate composition and country leverage measures support financing-structure statements; first-stage/overidentification diagnostics bound causal confidence.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: Empirical claims remain strong where robustness agrees, but the article retains residual endogeneity and does not directly observe the effectiveness of political leverage.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: Trade, aid, investment, intergovernmental, and bank-country leverage are kept distinct.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: Weak/partial empirical support for some leverage channels is retained instead of collapsing all political influence into one mechanism.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Large infrastructure/project-finance deals in developing economies; debt-side setting; syndicate-size/partner boundaries.
rhetoric.limitations: Residual endogeneity, mediocre first-stage fit on some dimensions, unobserved leverage effectiveness, and generalizability beyond project finance are explicit.
rhetoric.implications: Observed lender/partner selection and inferred effectiveness of that selection are different Finance claims.
anti_patterns: Do not equate observed syndicate composition with proven effectiveness of political leverage.
Do not generalize project-finance debt structure to all corporate finance.

atomic_observations.observation: Observed financing structure can be strongly supported while the effectiveness of the proposed strategic mechanism remains less directly identified.
The project-finance/developing-economy setting belongs in the subject when it bounds generalization.
Finance language can distinguish lead arranger, syndicate composition, non-local debt, project finance, and creditor leverage.
Instrument-strength and residual-endogeneity qualifications should remain adjacent to the strongest causal interpretation.

official_admissions.title: Has persistence persisted in private equity? Evidence from buyout and venture capital funds

full_text.source: Elsevier open-access article plus NBER full working-paper version
full_text.scope: All substantive argumentative sections available in the full article/public full-version were reviewed: framing/theory, design/method, main results, robustness or heterogeneity where present, discussion/conclusion, and limitations/boundaries. Tables/equations were inspected when needed to calibrate claims.

summary_architecture: replace hindsight measure with information available at fundraising
rhetoric.evidence_order: The paper's central rhetorical move is to change the information set: final/latest fund performance is compared with what an investor actually knew when choosing the next fund.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Performance rankings become economically meaningful only after measurement is aligned with the actual fundraising decision date.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: The study is not primarily causal; its strength lies in avoiding look-ahead/hindsight information when evaluating persistence.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: Buyout and VC differ; pre-2001/post-2000 cohorts differ; final versus fundraising-date metrics differ.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: Little/no buyout persistence under decision-time information is retained even though ex-post measures reproduce conventional persistence.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Institutional-investor Burgiss cash-flow data; U.S. buyout/VC funds; performance measure and fundraising date define the information set.
rhetoric.limitations: Observed persistence depends materially on performance timing/measurement and fund type.
rhetoric.implications: Private-capital evaluation should separate final or most-recent performance from the NAV/cash-flow information actually observable when a commitment decision is made.
anti_patterns: Do not evaluate a historical decision using information that became available only later.
Do not use ex-post quartile status as if investors knew it at fundraising.

atomic_observations.observation: Evaluation of a decision or predictive relationship should use information available at the decision point; ex-post outcomes can create hindsight performance that was not actionable ex ante.
Final fund performance and fundraising-date performance are non-equivalent measures because they contain different information sets.
Private-capital prose should distinguish paid-in cash flows, interim/fundraising-date performance, final performance, GP persistence, buyout, and venture capital.
Persistence changes by fund type and fundraising era; conventional wisdom should be written conditionally.

official_admissions.title: Corporate bond liquidity before and after the onset of the subprime crisis

full_text.source: Elsevier open-access version of record / public author full version
full_text.scope: All substantive argumentative sections available in the full article/public full-version were reviewed: framing/theory, design/method, main results, robustness or heterogeneity where present, discussion/conclusion, and limitations/boundaries. Tables/equations were inspected when needed to calibrate claims.

summary_architecture: identify crisis onset as regime shift
rhetoric.evidence_order: The crisis shift is stated first, then the paper separates persistence and magnitude by rating segment and issuer/underwriter condition.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Liquidity's contribution to spreads is quantified separately from total spread changes; rating-level paths carry the main interpretation.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: The crisis/natural-experiment timing strengthens attribution of regime change, but liquidity and credit-risk components still require measurement decomposition.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_time: Investment-grade liquidity deterioration is slower/more persistent; speculative-grade effect is stronger/more short-lived; financial issuers and distressed underwriters differ.
rhetoric.null_or_nonresult_language: Flight-to-quality is explicitly confined to AAA rather than generalized across all investment grade.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Corporate bond market 2005–2009; TRACE-based liquidity measure; subprime crisis; rating groups and underwriter distress.
rhetoric.limitations: Illiquidity measurement and crisis-specific period constrain universal spread interpretation.
rhetoric.implications: Credit conditions should separate total corporate-bond spread, liquidity component, rating segment, persistence, and intermediary distress.
anti_patterns: Do not call wider corporate spreads purely credit risk when liquidity contributes materially.
Do not generalize a AAA flight-to-quality result to every investment-grade bond.

atomic_observations.observation: A financial spread should be decomposed into economically distinct components when those components change differently across regimes.
Crisis effects differ in magnitude and persistence by credit-quality segment; regime and rating belong in the thesis.
Finance language should distinguish corporate spread, liquidity premium, rating quality, underwriter distress, issuer distress, and flight to quality.
A result confined to AAA bonds must remain grammatically confined to AAA bonds.

atomic_observation_registry.observation: A variable's level and an imposed change in that variable are different evidentiary objects and can have different or opposite relationships with outcomes; prose should not treat them as interchangeable.
A literature can support a broad directional relationship while remaining too heterogeneous to supply a reliable policy effect size.
Finance language should distinguish bank capital levels, regulatory ratios, capital requirements, and changes in requirements.
Meta-analytic synthesis should decompose capital constructs and empirical contexts before stating an aggregate lending conclusion.
Finance prose can describe working capital and fixed investment as competing uses of finite internal cash, making allocation pressure explicit.
Liquidity changes the strength of the financing-constraint effect; the buffer condition belongs in the interpretation.
Predicted moderator behavior can support a mechanism without fully identifying it.
Hidden-bias and sample-composition limits should be attached to the causal/channel claim they constrain.
An intervention can succeed on one financial objective and deteriorate another; evaluation must remain outcome-specific.
Short-run deterioration followed by medium-term relief should be stated as a time path.
Government-backed finance can be described through profitability additionality, leverage, financial burden, debt sustainability, and business-continuity tradeoffs.
Strong intervention verbs are justified only for outcomes supported by the quasi-experimental design.
A group can have a worse baseline state without experiencing a larger response to a shock; level disparity and shock sensitivity are separate claims.
Crisis and post-crisis periods change the financing interpretation, so the temporal regime belongs in the claim.
Cash accumulation can be described as a financing buffer and potential substitute for debt during recovery.
The conclusion should retain the established-German-firm sample rather than becoming a universal SME claim.
An aggregate policy regime can produce heterogeneous borrower-level outcomes; the borrower/jurisdiction condition must remain explicit.
Finance prose can distinguish policy stance, bank transmission, borrower leverage, credit constraint, discouraged borrowing, and jurisdiction stress.
'Little evidence' for one risk channel is narrower than evidence that the channel is absent.
Alternative measures of policy stance and firm risk are non-equivalent proxies and should not be silently merged.
A financing instrument's usefulness is function-specific: tax incentives, guarantees, credit lines, and equity address different funding jobs.
Collateral, paperwork, price of credit, guarantees, credit lines, and equity are distinct Finance predicates/objects, not one generic 'access' variable.
Self-perceived financing constraints and observed balance-sheet constraints are non-equivalent measurements.
Measurement limitations should constrain policy/cause language exactly where subjective survey responses are doing the evidentiary work.
A change in a balance-sheet stock can arise from different underlying transactions; aggregate stock growth should not be assigned to a specific flow without decomposition.
Observed loan balances do not reveal all underlying origination versus commitment-draw mechanics without additional data.
Finance language should distinguish committed credit, line drawdown, new origination, liquidity demand, deposit inflow, and bank funding capacity.
'No robust evidence' is the correct form for unstable bank-condition relationships.
Finance prose can distinguish liquidity stress, delinquency, bank-credit access, trade-credit substitution, public support, and operational adjustment.
A broad stress outcome becomes interpretable when decomposed into financing-source and operational responses.
The relevant subject is previously credit-rationed SMEs during a pandemic regime, not firms universally.
Pre-shock status strengthens sequencing but does not by itself identify every response mechanism.
A single observed transaction outcome can be jointly generated by two sides of a market; when evidence separates them, supply-side and demand-side drivers should remain distinct.
Finance language should distinguish borrower demand/exposure, lender supply/exposure, syndicated quantity, price/spread, and cross-border channel.
Decomposing an aggregate lending outcome by market side prevents mechanism misattribution.
Distinct borrower and lender channels justify separate grammatical claims before total lending interpretation.
Partial mediation should preserve the residual direct relationship and possibility of additional mechanisms.
A dominant channel does not imply a competing channel is absent.
Corporate cash can be framed as precautionary liquidity linked to external credit access, debt capacity, and banking-market structure.
A financing relationship that strengthens over historical subperiods should not be summarized as a fixed timeless coefficient.
Main effects and interactions can point in different directions; the combined state is not a restatement of either component alone.
Finance language should distinguish precautionary cash, inflation risk, policy uncertainty, interest burden, and joint macro-risk exposure.
Mixed empirical signs should outrank a simple theoretical narrative about uncertainty.
Dynamic-panel robustness strengthens association but does not automatically justify structural-shock language.
Pooled baseline and contextual moderators should be synthesized as separate evidence layers.
Meta-analytic association supports a robust pattern but not causal mechanism language.
Publication, selection, omitted-variable, and causal limits are most useful when tied to the exact inference they bound.
Finance access should distinguish application/approval, rejection, interest terms, and borrower selection rather than one generic access outcome.
Observed financing structure can be strongly supported while the effectiveness of the proposed strategic mechanism remains less directly identified.
The project-finance/developing-economy setting belongs in the subject when it bounds generalization.
Finance language can distinguish lead arranger, syndicate composition, non-local debt, project finance, and creditor leverage.
Instrument-strength and residual-endogeneity qualifications should remain adjacent to the strongest causal interpretation.
Evaluation of a decision or predictive relationship should use information available at the decision point; ex-post outcomes can create hindsight performance that was not actionable ex ante.
Final fund performance and fundraising-date performance are non-equivalent measures because they contain different information sets.
Private-capital prose should distinguish paid-in cash flows, interim/fundraising-date performance, final performance, GP persistence, buyout, and venture capital.
Persistence changes by fund type and fundraising era; conventional wisdom should be written conditionally.
A financial spread should be decomposed into economically distinct components when those components change differently across regimes.
Crisis effects differ in magnitude and persistence by credit-quality segment; regime and rating belong in the thesis.
Finance language should distinguish corporate spread, liquidity premium, rating quality, underwriter distress, issuer distress, and flight to quality.
A result confined to AAA bonds must remain grammatically confined to AAA bonds.

finance_batch_001.interpretation: The large first batch adds substantial Finance-conditioned vocabulary and strongly reinforces Market-derived analytical machinery. Two observations are currently strong enough to label new universal machinery: level-versus-change/intervention distinction and baseline-state-versus-shock-sensitivity distinction, plus decision-time-information-set evaluation. Two-sided-market and stock-change/underlying-flow observations remain provisional until another Finance batch or later domains reinforce them.
finance_batch_001.reason: Finance conceptual coverage is not yet complete; the batch is foundation-building.

new_universal_candidates.name: Level versus change/intervention
new_universal_candidates.observation: A variable's level and an imposed change in that variable are different evidentiary objects and can support different or opposite outcome relationships.

new_universal_candidates.name: Baseline state versus shock sensitivity
new_universal_candidates.observation: A group can begin from a worse baseline without responding more strongly to a subsequent shock; baseline disparity and shock elasticity are separate claims.

new_universal_candidates.name: Decision-time information set
new_universal_candidates.observation: Historical evaluation should use information that was actually available at the decision point; ex-post final outcomes can create hindsight relationships that were not actionable ex ante.

provisional_candidates.name: Balance-sheet stock change versus underlying transaction flow
provisional_candidates.observation: An observed stock increase can be generated by different underlying flows, such as new origination versus drawing an already committed credit line.

provisional_candidates.name: Two-sided transaction decomposition
provisional_candidates.observation: Observed financing quantity/price can jointly reflect borrower demand and lender supply; the two sides should remain separate when the design distinguishes them.
